references.text: The parallel text in Mark where the woman came trembling and fell down before Jesus and told him the whole truth, just as in Luke's account.
The parallel text in Matthew about the woman with bleeding who touched Jesus' cloak and was healed.
The immediate context where the woman touched his cloak and was immediately healed — what she now confesses publicly in verse 47.
Jesus asks who touched him, and realizes that power had gone out from him — this leads to the woman's confession in verse 47.
Jesus' answer to the woman after her public confession: 'Your faith has saved you; go in peace.'
Peter and John declare that they cannot help speaking about what they have seen and heard — a similar principle of bearing public witness to God's works.
The psalmist praises the Lord in the great assembly — the woman confessed her healing publicly before all the people, in a similar way.
Those whom the Lord has rescued shall tell it — an encouragement to bear public witness to God's salvation and healing, as the woman did.
'Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for my soul' — the woman told all the people what Jesus had done for her.
Trembling and awe in God's presence — the woman came trembling (τρέμουσα) when she realized she was not hidden from Jesus.
